create.name: Rodger Kamenetz
create.bio:
Rodger Kamenetz is an American poet, author and teacher whose work brings together poetry, dreams and Jewish spiritual life. Born in Baltimore and educated at Yale, Johns Hopkins and Stanford, he spent many years at Louisiana State University, holding posts in both English and Religious Studies, and retired as a distinguished professor. His most widely read book is The Jew in the Lotus, an account of a group of rabbis who travelled to Dharamsala to talk with the Dalai Lama, which was later made into a PBS documentary. Its sequel, Stalking Elijah, about his meetings with Jewish mystical teachers across America, won a National Jewish Book Award, and his other books include Burnt Books, The History of Last Night's Dream and Seeing into the Life of Things.

With colleagues he developed Natural Dreamwork, an approach that sets interpretation aside and asks the dreamer to slow down and feel the images of a dream as living encounters. From his home in New Orleans he now gives much of his time to one-to-one dream sessions for people who want spiritual direction through their dreams. He also teaches through lectures, synagogue weekends, contemplative retreats and online classes, including a past Natural Dreamwork course with The Shift Network, often weaving blessing practices and close attention to the natural world into the work.

books.title: The History of Last Night's Dream
books.author: Rodger Kamenetz
books.description: Part memoir and part argument, this book follows his turn towards dreams as a path to the soul and questions the habit of explaining dreams away. Published by HarperOne.

books.title: Stalking Elijah
books.author: Rodger Kamenetz
books.description: The sequel to The Jew in the Lotus, in which he travels across America to meet contemporary Jewish mystical teachers while looking for his own way of practice. It won a National Jewish Book Award.

courses.title: One-to-One Natural Dreamwork Sessions
courses.description: Private sessions in the dreamwork approach he founded: you send recent dreams beforehand and then revisit their images slowly together, staying with what is felt rather than interpreting. Sessions with him are arranged by writing to his dreamwork address.
